description: Component pattern rules for frontend implementation step. Ensures UX quality in generated code.

rules.rule: Implement in TWO phases: (1) Skeleton — app shell with navigation, routing, shared components (toast, dialog, loading spinner). (2) Per-module — implement each module's list/detail/form views consuming the skeleton.
rules.verify: index.html has nav element; app.js has route handling for all modules.

rules.rule: Create reusable shared components BEFORE module code: showToast(message, type), showConfirmDialog(message, onConfirm), showLoading(container), showEmptyState(container, message, actionLabel, onAction).
rules.verify: app.js defines showToast, showConfirmDialog or confirm() calls, loading indicator function.

rules.rule: Each module MUST implement: list view (with empty state), create form (with validation), edit form, delete button (with confirmation dialog). Do NOT skip any module from the spec.
rules.verify: app.js has fetch+render+create+update+delete handlers for every module.

rules.rule: After every API call: show loading during fetch, show toast on success/failure, show empty state when list is empty, show inline validation errors on form submit.
rules.verify: Every fetch() call has .then(showToast success) and .catch(showToast error) or equivalent.

rules.rule: Multi-module apps: persistent sidebar or top navigation listing ALL modules. Active module highlighted. Click navigates without page reload.
rules.verify: index.html has nav/sidebar with links to all modules; app.js highlights active.

rules.rule: MANDATORY: ALL user-controlled strings inserted into HTML via innerHTML or template literals MUST go through escapeHtml(). This includes: customer names, ticket titles, descriptions, comments, usernames, AND modal dialog messages (showConfirmDialog message parameter). Never trust data from the API.
rules.verify: grep 'innerHTML.*\${' and confirm every interpolated user value is wrapped in escapeHtml(). showConfirmDialog must call escapeHtml(message) before innerHTML assignment.

rules.rule: Do NOT interpolate user-controlled status/priority/type values directly into HTML class attributes. Use a whitelist/map: const STATUS_CLASSES = {open:'badge-open', closed:'badge-closed', ...}; then class="${STATUS_CLASSES[status] || 'badge-default'}". Never class="badge ${status.toLowerCase()}".
rules.verify: No template literals of the form class="...${userValue}..." with raw user values. Use lookup tables.

rules.rule: When an async operation (e.g. loadOptions) appends to a DOM element inside a modal, check that the modal is still open before appendChild. Pattern: const modal = currentModal; await loadOptions(); if (modal !== currentModal) return;
rules.verify: Async append operations guard against modal being closed mid-fetch.
